title: Chicken Thighs With Hot Honey Carrots on a Sheet Pan
description: By Melissa Clark: Roasting root vegetables and chicken together on a sheet-pan is a classic dinner move. As the chicken cooks, the skin browns and crisps, and the fat renders, contributing flavor and richness to the vegetables in the pan. Here, bone-in chicken legs are surrounded by carrots and red onions, which get especially sweet and soft as they caramelize in the oven. A hot honey glaze adds verve and spice, while crushed fennel or coriander seeds lend a gentle perfume. Serve this with warm bread to soak up all the flavorful drippings.
ingredients: 2 ½ pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
1 ¼ teaspoons fine sea salt, plus more as needed
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more as needed
2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice, plus more for serving
1 ½ pounds carrots, cut into ¾-inch pieces
1 ½ tablespoons hot honey (or regular honey mixed with a big pinch of cayenne)
1 small red onion, halved and thinly sliced into half-moons
1 teaspoon fennel or coriander seeds, coarsely crushed (or use ½ teaspoon each)
½ cup chopped fresh basil, mint, cilantro, dill or a combination
directions: Line a sheet pan with parchment paper if you like (this helps with clean up). Season chicken all over with ¼ teaspoon salt.
Finely grate 1 garlic clove and put in a small bowl. Stir in the olive oil, lemon juice and paprika.
Put the chicken on the prepared pan and pour or smear the garlic mixture all over it, tossing to coat. Arrange the pieces skin-side up.

Add the carrots, remaining 4 garlic cloves and the thyme sprigs to the pan, spreading everything out around the chicken. Season carrots lightly with salt and drizzle with a little more olive oil. Transfer pan to the oven and roast for 20 minutes.

Drizzle chicken and carrots with honey. Stir the onions and fennel seeds into the carrots, but don’t disturb the chicken. Drizzle everything with a little more oil. Continue to roast until the chicken is golden, and the onions and carrots are tender, 20 to 25 minutes longer.

Transfer chicken to plates. Stir the vegetables in the pan, scraping up all the delicious browned bits from the bottom. Taste and add salt, if needed, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice, if you like. Top with herbs and serve.
